# U.S. Language Services LLC

> Serving law firms across the United States, U.S. Language Services LLC provides accurate and reliable certified translations in over 35 languages. Our commitment to precision, efficiency, and exceptional customer service has made us a trusted partner for the legal community nationwide.


## Services

- [Certified Translation](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/certified-translation/): Certified Translation Services for Law Firms and Individuals. USCIS Acceptance Guaranteed. 35 languages.

- [Standard Translation](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/standard-translation/): Professional human translation services in 35 languages. Excellent quality delivered fast. Available 24/7. Native translators. ATA Certified.

## Online-store

- [Order Your Translation](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/order-your-translation/): Online translation store available 24/7. Certified Translation $39.00/page or $0.12 per word. 35 Languages supported.

## Meet-the-team
- [Meet The Team](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/meet-the-team/): Our customer service and our social values define us. We believe languages are bridges between cultures, not social barriers.

  team_members:
    - name: Alyssa Morse-Salvati
      title: Director
      bio: Originally from the Boston area and a graduate of Tufts University, Alyssa studied translation at NYU and has more than 15 years of experience in the field. She has translated legal and financial texts for some of the largest firms in Europe.
      enjoys: Alyssa has always been fascinated by other cultures and languages. Her passion began at age 10, when she took her first solo trip to Venezuela to visit a friend. She later met Jaime while studying Spanish in Madrid, and the rest is history. In her free time, she enjoys reading, working out, and spending time with her dog Macarena (yes, like the song).

    - name: Jaime A. Carrión
      title: Technical Director
      bio: Jaime has over 15 years of experience in web development and founded his own translation company in Spain. He studied design at the Center for Digital Imaging Arts at Boston University and manages the technical operations of U.S. Language Services.
      enjoys: Born in Ecuador and having lived in Spain and the U.S., Jaime feels connected to all three countries. He loves learning about different cultures and sharing what he learns. When not working, he tends to his cactus garden, listens to podcasts, runs, flies his drone, or plays Factorio.

    - name: Anthony Rodríguez
      title: Project Manager
      bio: Anthony holds a degree in Business Administration from Hardin-Simmons University and is bilingual in English and Spanish. He excels at coordinating translation projects with translators in more than 20 countries.
      enjoys: Passionate about continuous learning, Anthony often enrolls in courses on topics like business, finance, and international commerce. In his free time, he enjoys weightlifting, attending concerts, and cheering for Real Madrid.

    - name: Quoc Dung Hoang (William)
      title: Assistant Project Manager
      bio: William graduated from Hardin-Simmons University and brings strong cross-cultural experience from working in international environments. Fluent in English and Vietnamese, he combines analytical and communication skills with a background in IT and management.
      enjoys: William enjoys exploring new technologies and coding. Outside of work, he likes watching wrestling, playing soccer at his local club, and reading books.

    - name: Jesús Rodríguez Vidal
      title: Assistant Project Manager
      bio: Jesús is a trained nursing assistant with experience across multiple industries. His hands-on background includes production and machinery operations, demonstrating adaptability and technical competence.
      enjoys: A curious lifelong learner, Jesús explores topics such as economics, politics, behavioral sciences, and nonverbal communication. In his spare time, he goes to the gym, plays basketball, and enjoys volleyball.

## Movements-we-support

- [Movements We Support](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/movements-we-support/): U.S. Language Services is deeply committed to supporting movements that advance equality, human rights, and social justice. We believe silence and inaction perpetuate inequality. Real change requires participation from everyone, including the business community.

  principles:
    statement: Equality requires initiative and courage. We stand firmly for causes that make our communities safer, fairer, and more compassionate for all. Change takes collective effort, and we are proud to support organizations that share these values.

  supported_movements:
    - name: Racial Justice
      description: Systemic racism must be dismantled to ensure equal rights and opportunities for all communities of color.

        description: A nonprofit racial justice organization driving corporate and government leaders to create a more humane and equitable world for Black communities and beyond.
        website: https://colorofchange.org

    - name: Ending Gun Violence

      organization:
        name: Everytown for Gun Safety
        description: The largest gun violence prevention organization in the U.S., uniting over 8 million Americans to end gun violence through advocacy and public safety reforms.
        website: https://everytown.org

    - name: Universal Access to All Knowledge

        website: https://freedom.press

    - name: Animal Cruelty

## Documents

- [Documents](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/documents/): U.S. Language Services provides certified and professional document translation in more than 35 languages, covering legal, academic, medical, financial, and personal documents. Our team of expert translators ensures accuracy, confidentiality, and compliance with official requirements for USCIS, courts, universities, and government agencies.
  Use Cases: Individuals, law firms, and organizations rely on our document translation services for immigration filings, legal procedures, international studies, employment abroad, business operations, and official certifications. Every certified translation includes proper formatting and a Certificate of Accuracy.

## Guides-resources
- [Guides & Resources](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/): Practical guides to help you understand when a certified translation is required and how to navigate immigration, naturalization, academic recognition, working or studying abroad, personal finance, and retirement planning.

### Immigration
- [What Is An Apostille?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-an-apostille/): Discover what an apostille is, how to obtain and translate one, and its role in authenticating documents for international use.
- [Understanding NDAs in Translation Services: What You Need to Know](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/understanding-ndas-in-translation-services-what-you-need-to-know/): Understand how an NDA helps you safeguard legal, medical, or business documents during translation projects.
- [How Can I Get a Green Card?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/how-can-i-get-a-green-card/): Learn how to apply for a Green Card, the U.S. permanent residence card every foreigner seeks.
- [What Is A Marriage Green Card?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-a-marriage-green-card/): Learn the 3 steps to apply for a marriage Green Card, as well as other important information.
- [What Is Form I-130?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-form-i-130/): If you are interested in being sponsored or sponsoring a family member for a Green Card, learn how the I-130 form (Petition for Alien relative) can establish a valid family relationship.
- [What Is Form I-485?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-form-i-485/): Adjusting your immigration status is vital to staying in the country while your immigration paperwork is processing. Learn how to fill out form I-485 to maintain good immigration status.
- [What Is Form I-864?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-form-i-864/): Learn how to fill out form I-864, the Affidavit of support, and how it helps you show financial support from your sponsor during your immigration process.
- [What Is Form I-765?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-form-i-765/): Learn how to fill out form I-765 which allows you to request your Employment Authorization Document.
- [What Is Form I-131?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-form-i-131/): Learn how to fill out form I-131 which would allow you to leave the U.S. and visit your home country while waiting for your Green Card to be approved.
- [What Is Form I-751?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-form-i-751/): Learn how to fill out form I-751 and how it can help you remove your conditional permanent resident (CR-1) status.
- [What Is Form G-1145?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-form-g-1145/): Use form G-1145 to request an email or text notification from the USCIS to find out if your immigration application is accepted for processing.
- [What Is Form I-90?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-form-i-90/): Use form I-90 (Application to Replace Permanent Resident Card) to renew or replace your Green Card if lost or damaged. Learn when and how to file form I-90.
- [What Is A Green Card Number?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-a-green-card-number/): What does my Green Card number mean and where can I find it? Here is a quick run down on everything you should know about your Green Card.
- [What Is My Alien Registration Number?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-my-alien-registration-number/): Learn what your Alien Registration Number, or USCIS Number, is, its uses, and how it differs from other forms of ID.
- [What Is The Income Requirement For A Green Card Sponsor?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-the-income-requirement-for-a-green-card-sponsor/): You only need to have a yearly income of $22,887 (125% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines) to be a Green Card sponsor. Check what you need to show that you can financially sponsor your loved ones.
- [How Much Does it Cost to Obtain a Green Card?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/how-much-does-it-cost-to-obtain-a-green-card/): Green Card filing-fees start at $1,200, but vary case to case. Learn about the different costs and filing-fees for a Green Card to anticipate your expenses.
- [How Long Does the Green Card Process Take on Average?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/how-long-does-the-green-card-process-take-on-average/): Processing times for Green Card applications vary case to case. Learn how long it will take for your Green Card application to be processed and what can cause delays.
- [What is the Process For Checking the Status of a Green Card Application?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-the-process-for-checking-the-status-of-a-green-card-application/): Learn about the process and how you can easily check your Green Card application status online.
- [What is the Process for Renewing an Expired Green Card?](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/what-is-the-process-for-renewing-an-expired-green-card/): Do you know if you are eligible to renew your expired Green Card? Learn how, when, and what you need to renew your expired Green Card.
- [How to Obtain a Replacement for a Lost or Stolen Green Card](https://www.uslanguageservices.com/guides-resources/how-to-obtain-a-replacement-for-a-lost-or-stolen-green-card/): Have you lost your Green Card or has it been stolen?
